evidence: spec/1.5.0.md:127-131 "`critical_path` is the longest chain, by count, of not-done epics joined by dependency edges and ending at a not-done member of the milestone's gate ... The heaviest such chain by summed estimate is reported only when every epic on every such chain, the gate members included, has an estimate"
finding: 'The heaviest such chain by summed estimate' reads two ways. (a) 'such chain' means any chain as defined in the previous sentence's genus (not-done epics joined by dependency edges ending at a not-done gate member), so the estimate path is the heaviest of all of them and may be shorter by count than `critical_path`; (b) 'such chain' means the longest-by-count chains, so the estimate only breaks ties among them. On a graph with a 3-epic chain of 10 minutes each and a 2-epic chain of 100 minutes each, (a) reports the 2-epic chain and (b) the 3-epic chain. The reporting precondition 'every epic on every such chain' inherits the same split: under (b) only the longest chains need estimates.

resolved.evidence: Decided at the review cap in spec/1.5.0-corrections.md C2 and carried into the implementing tasks' acceptance.

suggestion: Name the set: 'Of all chains of not-done epics ending at a not-done gate member, the heaviest by summed estimate is reported apart, only when every epic on any of them has an estimate.'

evidence: spec/1.5.0.md:140-142 "every write of a done record, a met record or a binding exits 2, the removals included: `tp epic done` and its `--undo`, `tp epic gate --met`, and `tp init --epic` and `tp set --epic`" vs :150-152 "`claimed`, `done` and `met` are written by their commands and by `tp epic import`, the migration; a writer that replaces a whole object (`set gates=`, a `--bulk` row) carries them over"
finding: The `TP_UNATTENDED` fence is stated as 'every write of a done record, a met record or a binding exits 2', then lists five commands. §8 names two more writers of `done` and `met`: `tp epic import` (the migration) and the whole-object writers (`set gates=`, a `--bulk` row) that carry them over. Read by its general clause, unattended `tp epic import` of a graph holding done/met records, and arguably every carry-over rewrite, exits 2; read by its list, they run. Two implementations disagree on whether `TP_UNATTENDED=1 tp epic import <graph with a done record>` exits 2, and row 14 does not decide it.

resolved.evidence: Decided at the review cap in spec/1.5.0-corrections.md C3 and carried into the implementing tasks' acceptance.

suggestion: Make the list closed ('these commands exit 2') or add `tp epic import` explicitly to or out of the fence; state that a carry-over is not a write of the record.

evidence: spec/1.5.0.md:110-111 'lists the work epics that can start: in an open milestone, not done, every dependency `done`, no bound file, no claim, not a condition' vs :117-118 '`tp epic ready` and `tp epic status` name each claim's holder, the answer to "who has it" when several agents work.'
finding: `tp epic ready` is defined to list only work epics with 'no claim', yet the same section says '`tp epic ready` and `tp epic status` name each claim's holder'. A claimed epic is excluded from the ready list, so the ready output has no row on which to name a holder. Two correct implementations diverge: one adds a separate claimed list to `tp epic ready` (a list the criteria never define), the other names no holder in `tp epic ready` at all, which contradicts the sentence. The holder sentence is what answers 'who has it', so the choice changes what an agent sees before picking work.

resolved.evidence: Decided at the review cap in spec/1.5.0-corrections.md C1 and carried into the implementing tasks' acceptance.

suggestion: Either say `tp epic ready` lists the claimed epics that otherwise meet the criteria apart, with their holder (as it already lists the operator-waiting set apart), or drop `tp epic ready` from the holder sentence and leave it to `tp epic status`.

evidence: spec/1.5.0.md:110-111 "lists the work epics that can start: in an open milestone, not done, every dependency `done`, no bound file, no claim, not a condition" vs :117-118 "`tp epic ready` and `tp epic status` name each claim's holder"
finding: `tp epic ready` lists work epics with 'no claim', yet the same bullet says '`tp epic ready` and `tp epic status` name each claim's holder'. A claimed epic is excluded from the ready list, so there is no row in it on which to name a holder. Two correct implementations diverge: (a) `tp epic ready` adds a separate claimed list (epics that would be ready but for the claim) with each holder; (b) `tp epic ready` shows no claims at all and only `tp epic status` names holders. A test asserting the holder appears in `tp epic ready` output passes one and fails the other.

resolved.evidence: Decided at the review cap in spec/1.5.0-corrections.md C1 and carried into the implementing tasks' acceptance.

suggestion: Say where `tp epic ready` shows claims, e.g. 'claimed epics that otherwise meet the ready rules are listed apart with their holder', or drop `tp epic ready` from the holder sentence.

evidence: spec/1.5.0.md:181 "`tp epic status` reports the not-done epics before a done one as the critical path by count, the done epic cutting the chain | the chain with b done and A's gate on a"; :127-128 "ending at a not-done member of the milestone's gate; a done epic cuts a chain"
finding: Row 12 expects 'the not-done epics before a done one as the critical path', plural, on 'the chain with b done and A's gate on a'. In a→b→c→d, a depends on b (row 3 has b blocked by c). §7's path must end at a not-done gate member (a) and a done epic cuts it, so the only chain is [a], one epic; c and d lie beyond the cut and end at no gate member. A tester reading the row writes an assertion for several epics (e.g. [d, c] or [c, a]) that the §7 definition never produces.

resolved.evidence: Decided at the review cap in spec/1.5.0-corrections.md C5 and carried into the implementing tasks' acceptance.

suggestion: State the expected path: 'reports [a] as the critical path, b cutting it from c and d', or move the gate so the expected chain has more than one epic.

evidence: spec/1.5.0.md:52-57 'a bound spec edited after its release falls back to `audit`, and its epic is in progress again ... `done_at` is ... the time of the audit round that brought the last bound file to `release` most recently' vs :123-124 '`throughput`, epics whose current `done_at` falls in each ISO week'
finding: §3 defines `done_at` for a bound epic as 'the time of the audit round that brought the last bound file to `release` most recently', a value that still exists after the epic reopens (its spec edited, phase back to `audit`). §7's `throughput` counts 'epics whose current `done_at` falls in each ISO week' without restricting to epics whose status is `done`. One implementation counts a reopened, not-done epic in its old week; another counts only `done` epics. The stated intent ('counts in its later week') covers re-done epics but not epics that are currently reopened.

resolved.evidence: Decided at the review cap in spec/1.5.0-corrections.md C4 and carried into the implementing tasks' acceptance.

suggestion: Say `done_at` is defined only while the epic's status is `done`, so `throughput` counts done epics only.

evidence: spec/1.5.0.md:33-35 (binding refusals: absent id, condition, done record only); :55 'A claim on an epic with a bound file is ignored.'; :115-118 'it exits 1 when a claim exists, and on a condition, a done epic or an epic with a bound file ... `--release` removes it. `tp epic ready` and `tp epic status` name each claim's holder'
finding: A claim can outlive a binding: §2 does not refuse binding a claimed epic, and the claim stays in the graph (§3: 'A claim on an epic with a bound file is ignored'). §7 then makes `tp epic claim` exit 1 'on an epic with a bound file', which reads as covering `--release` too, so the stale claim can never be removed, while `tp epic status` 'name[s] each claim's holder'. One implementation reports a holder for a `specced`/`in_progress` epic whose claim §3 ignores; another hides it. Neither can let the operator clear it if `--release` is refused.

resolved.evidence: Decided at the review cap in spec/1.5.0-corrections.md C6 and carried into the implementing tasks' acceptance.

suggestion: State that `--release` is accepted on any epic carrying a claim, and that holders are named only for epics whose status is `claimed` (or that binding drops the claim from the reported view).

evidence: spec/1.5.0.md:140-144 'every write of a done record, a met record or a binding exits 2 ... A unit escalates them as the decisions `epic-done`, `gate-met` and `epic-binding`'; spec/1.5.0.md:150-151 '`claimed`, `done` and `met` are written by their commands and by `tp epic import`, the migration'; internal/cli/epic_unattended_test.go:14-40 (TestEpicWriters_UnattendedRefusesEveryWriter) pins `tp epic import ... --force` under TP_UNATTENDED to exit 2 with 'tp escalate --decision other'.
finding: The round-3 repair turned the fence into a rule over every write of a done or met record and named the decisions those writes escalate as. §8 says `tp epic import` also writes `done` and `met`. Since v1.3.0, import has been fenced as a graph writer that escalates as `other`, and a test pins that. Both readings still exit 2. They differ on the decision name: one implementation keeps import on `other`, and another, following 'every write ... escalates them as `epic-done`/`gate-met`', changes it to `epic-done` or `gate-met` when the payload carries those records. That breaks the settled test or leaves the new rule unmet for import. Row 14 does not cover import.

resolved.evidence: Decided at the review cap in spec/1.5.0-corrections.md C3 and carried into the implementing tasks' acceptance.

suggestion: Limit the escalation sentence to the commands it lists, or add that `tp epic import` keeps its v1.3.0 fence and its `other` decision whatever records it carries.

evidence: spec/1.5.0.md:56-57 "`done_at` is ... the time of the audit round that brought the last bound file to `release` most recently: it moves when an epic reopens and is done again"; :123-124 "`throughput`, epics whose current `done_at` falls in each ISO week"
finding: `throughput` counts 'epics whose current `done_at` falls in each ISO week'. §3 defines `done_at` for a bound epic as the time of the audit round that brought its last bound file to `release` most recently, which still exists while the epic has reopened and is `in_progress`. Whether a currently not-done epic is counted in its last done week is left open: one implementation counts every epic with a `done_at`, another only epics whose status is `done`. A fixture with a released spec edited afterwards tells them apart.

resolved.evidence: Decided at the review cap in spec/1.5.0-corrections.md C4 and carried into the implementing tasks' acceptance.

suggestion: Say 'done epics whose `done_at` falls in each ISO week', or state that `done_at` is absent while the epic is not done.
